items.markingKey: (a) M1 Pythagoras; A1 magnitude; A1 direction [3] (b) M1 F = ma; A1 value [2] (c) B1 equal and opposite to the resultant [1]

items.stem: A pebble is projected vertically upwards with speed 10 m s⁻¹ from a point 15 m above the ground. Find the time taken to reach the ground.
items.markingKey: M1 −15 = ut − 5t²; M1 solves the quadratic; A1 time [3]

items.stem: A curve has parametric equations x = t² − 2, y = 2t³ + 3t. (a) Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where t = −1. (b) Find the value of t at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the y-axis.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 point (−1, −5); M1 gradient −9/2; A1 y = −(9/2)x − 19/2 [3] (b) M1 dx/dt = 0 with dy/dt ≠ 0; A1 t = 0 [2]

items.stem: A particle starts from O with velocity 8 m s⁻¹ and moves with acceleration a = −3t² − 4t + 5 m s⁻² at time t s. Find its displacement from O when t = 2.
items.markingKey: M1 integrates a; A1 v; M1 integrates v; A1 s [4]

items.stem: A particle of mass 1 kg moving at 8 m s⁻¹ collides with a particle of mass 3 kg at rest. They coalesce. Find their common speed.

items.stem: A particle of mass 2 kg rests on a smooth plane inclined at α, where sin α = 3/5. Find the component of its weight down the plane.
items.markingKey: mg sin α.

items.stem: A particle has velocity v = −3t² + 18t − 24 m s⁻¹. Explain the difference between its velocity and its speed at t = 3.
items.answer: v = 3 m s⁻¹: the sign gives the direction; the speed is the magnitude, 3 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: The points A and B have position vectors −3i + j and −2i + 9j + 4k. Find the distance AB, giving your answer exactly.

items.stem: In a problem about two particles connected over a pulley, Kwame assumes that the string is inextensible. Explain how this assumption is used in the solution.
items.answer: Because the string is inextensible, both particles have the same magnitude of acceleration.
items.markingKey: B1 consequence; B1 how it simplifies the equations [2]

items.stem: Use logarithms to answer the following, giving non-exact answers correct to 3 significant figures. (a) Find the smallest integer n such that 0.9ⁿ < 0.05. (b) Solve the equation 5^(2x) − 11(5ˣ) + 30 = 0.

items.stem: A car passes a point A with speed 2 m s⁻¹ and accelerates uniformly at 2 m s⁻² for 6 s. It then travels at constant speed for 10 s before decelerating uniformly to rest in 5 s. (a) Find the maximum speed. (b) Find the distance travelled while accelerating. (c) Find the deceleration in the final stage. (d) Find the total distance from A to the point where it comes to rest.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 v = u + at; A1 speed [2] (b) M1 s = ut + (1/2)at²; A1 distance [2] (c) B1 value [1] (d) M1 adds the three stages; A1 total [2]

items.stem: The region R is bounded by the curve y = sin x cos³x, the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = π/2. (a) Use the substitution u = cos x to show that the area of R is ∫ from 1 to 0 of −u³ du. (b) Hence find the exact area of R. (c) Give the area correct to 3 significant figures.
items.answer: (a) du = −sin x dx; new limits 1 and 0 (b) 1/4 (c) 0.250
items.markingKey: (a) M1 replaces dx; A1 integrand; B1 limits [3] (b) M1 integrates; A1 exact answer [2] (c) B1 value [1]

items.markingKey: (a) B1 conjugate; M1 quadratic factor; A1 real root [3] (b) B1 modulus; B1 argument [2] (c) B1 both [1]

items.stem: The curve C has equation y = eˣ − 7x. (a) Find the exact coordinates of the stationary point of C. (b) Determine the nature of the stationary point. (c) Find the gradient of C at the point where x = 1, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 eˣ = 7; A1 x = ln 7; A1 y = 7 − 7 ln 7 [3] (b) M1 d²y/dx² = eˣ > 0; A1 minimum [2] (c) B1 −4.28 [1]

items.stem: A particle of mass 5 kg moves 40 m down a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at 30°. Its speed at the top is 4 m s⁻¹. The resistance to motion is constant at 10 N. items.markingKey: (a) M1 mg × d sin α; A1 value [2] (b) B1 value [1] (c) M1 work-energy equation; A1 speed [2] (d) B1 value [1]

items.stem: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx + 8, where a and b are constants. It is given that (x + 4) is a factor of p(x), and that when p(x) is divided by (x − 1) the remainder is 30. (a) Find the values of a and b. (b) Hence factorise p(x) completely.
Given that tan(A + B) = 5 and tan A = 1/3, find the exact value of tan B.
items.markingKey: M1 (1/3 + t)/(1 − 1/3t) = 5; M1 rearranges for t; A1 tan B = 7/4 [3]

items.stem: A lift of mass 600 kg carries a crate of mass 50 kg on its floor. The lift starts from rest and accelerates downwards at 2 m s⁻² for 2 s. (a) Find the normal contact force between the crate and the floor of the lift. (b) State the force exerted by the crate on the floor, and name the law used.
items.answer: (a) 400 N (b) 400 N downwards, Newton's third law
items.markingKey: (a) M1 crate alone; A1 value [2] (b) B1 value and direction; B1 law [2]

items.stem: Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = √(5 − ln xₙ) with x₁ = 2 to determine the root of ln x + x² − 5 = 0 correct to 3 decimal places. Give the result of each iteration to 5 decimal places.

items.stem: A particle A of mass 2 kg moving at 3 m s⁻¹ collides directly with a particle B of mass 1 kg at rest. After the collision A moves at 1.25 m s⁻¹ in its original direction. Find the speed of B after the collision.

items.markingKey: Chain rule: k/(1 + (kx)²).

items.stem: Explain the modelling assumptions made when particles of masses 7 kg and 1 kg hang over a smooth peg and the acceleration is found as 7.5 m s⁻².
items.answer: The string is light and inextensible (same tension, same acceleration magnitude), the peg is smooth (tension the same on both sides), the particles are point masses, and air resistance is ignored.
items.markingKey: B1 string assumptions; B1 smooth peg and particles [1]

items.stem: Find the exact value of ∫_0^1 6eˣ dx.
A particle has velocity v = 3t² − 18t + 15 m s⁻¹. Kwame uses v = u + at to find the acceleration over the first 2 s. Explain why this does not give the acceleration at t = 2.
items.answer: The acceleration varies (a = 6t − 18), so (v − u)/t gives only an average; at t = 2 the acceleration is −6 m s⁻².
items.markingKey: B1 acceleration not constant; B1 differentiates to find a at t [2]

items.stem: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 24 m s⁻¹ in 12 s. It travels at this speed for 30 s and then decelerates uniformly to rest in 5 s.
